text: For the choirmaster. A psalm of David.
The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands.
Day after day they pour forth speech; night after night they reveal knowledge.
There is no speech, there are no words, no sound of their voice is heard.

versions.text: There is no speech, there are no words; their voice is never heard.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew בְּלִי נִשְׁמָע קוֹלָם continues the series of negations describing wordless testimony; "never heard" overstates the negation and can be misread as contradicting the universal reach affirmed in the next verse. A footnote noting the alternative rendering "there is no place where their voice is not heard" would also be helpful.

text: Yet their line goes out through all the earth, their words to the ends of the world. In them he has pitched a tent for the sun,

versions.text: Yet their measure goes out through all the earth, their words to the ends of the world. In them he has pitched a tent for the sun,
versions.explanation: Hebrew קַוָּם means "their line/cord" (a measuring line, hence by extension their reach). "Their measure" is vague and does not read naturally aloud; "their line" preserves the image, and a footnote could note that ancient versions read "their voice/sound."

text: which comes out like a bridegroom from his chamber, rejoicing like a champion to run its course.
It rises at one end of the heavens and circles to the other; nothing is hidden from its heat.
The law of the LORD is perfect, reviving the soul. The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple.
The precepts of the LORD are right, giving joy to the heart. The commandment of the LORD is radiant, giving light to the eyes.
The fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever. The judgments of the LORD are true, and altogether righteous.
They are more desirable than gold, than much pure gold; sweeter than honey, than honey from the comb.
Moreover, by them your servant is warned; in keeping them there is great reward.

versions.text: By them your servant is warned; in keeping them there is great reward.
versions.explanation: The emphatic particle גַּם ("moreover, also") that opens the verse is untranslated; including it preserves the connective flow from the preceding verse and aids oral reading.

text: Who can discern his own errors? Cleanse me from my hidden faults.
Keep your servant also from willful sins; do not let them rule over me. Then I will be blameless, innocent of great transgression.
May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be pleasing in your sight, O LORD, my rock and my redeemer.
